AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2 (monster stream), copied verbatim per governing rule 3 and not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (globe_head.py:33-37). Same observable today, established by execution rather than assumed, on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (modify_power_amount) and relics/vambrace.py:26-40 / relics/paels_legion.py:36-43 (modify_block_multiplicative); all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, and a monster's starting power is self-applied with no card, so none of them can fire. sts2_rl/potions.py implements none of the four hooks. (b) HP-roll inversion -- the sim applies the power before the Niche roll and the game after it; of the 35 constructor-applied power classes only IllusionPower mentions max_hp at all and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581), never at apply time. (c) roll ordering -- MachineMonster.__init__ rolls the first move (state_machine.py:301) *before* the subclass applies its powers, and `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op: this unit's initial state is a MoveState, so monster_state_machine step 30's early return fires and the first roll evaluates no branch and reads no power. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic, potion or power that listens on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. RULE 7: the four relic files and powers.py cited above are NOT hashed by this record (powers.py IS hashed here for other entries); flagged explicitly as the shared finding instructs. ESCALATION CHECK: GlobeHead.cs:41-45 applies GalvanicPower 6m to itself and does nothing else; the amount matches _GALVANIC = 6 (globe_head.py:19). Galvanic afflicts the PLAYER's Power cards, so unlike a plain self-buff it reaches the player's deck -- but it does so through the power's own card-entered-combat listener, not through the apply, so the shared finding's clause (a) still covers it: no ported modify_power_amount / modify_block_* listener fires on a monster self-application. The unit's initial state is the MoveState SHOCKING_SLAP, so clause (c) is a sticky no-op. GlobeHead does not read hooks.combat from __init__.

GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: Node-by-node against GlobeHead.cs:47-60: three MoveStates with matching ids (THUNDER_STRIKE / SHOCKING_SLAP / GALVANIC_BURST), the same three-cycle SHOCKING_SLAP -> THUNDER_STRIKE -> GALVANIC_BURST -> SHOCKING_SLAP (GlobeHead.cs:53-55 vs globe_head.py:52-54) and the same INITIAL state, SHOCKING_SLAP (GlobeHead.cs:59 passes moveState2). No branch state at all, so no AddBranch integer and no MonsterAi draw. Intents match: MultiAttackIntent(6, 3) -> Intent(ATTACK, damage=6, hits=3); SingleAttackIntent(13)+DebuffIntent -> ATTACK 13 also=(DEBUFF,); SingleAttackIntent(16)+BuffIntent -> ATTACK 16 also=(BUFF,).

Thunder Strike is `DamageCmd.Attack(6).WithHitCount(3)` -- one attack command, three hits -- and the sim's _execute_attack(ctx, 6, 3) (monsters/base.py:107-118) brackets all three hits in a single before_attack/after_attack pair and breaks early if either combatant dies, which is the same shape as AttackCommand's BeforeAttack/AfterAttack bracket.
